'''''Disocactus ackermannii''''' commonly called '''red orchid cactus''' is an [[epiphyte|epiphytic]] [[cactus]] from tropical forests in the states of [[Veracruz]] and [[Oaxaca]], Mexico. In cultivation, it has been confused with [[Disocactus × jenkinsonii|''Disocactus'' × ''jenkinsonii'']], a hybrid between ''[[Disocactus phyllanthoides|D. phyllanthoides]]'' and ''[[Disocactus speciosus|D. speciosus]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Heath|first=P. V.|date=1989|title=The strange and curious tale of the true and false ''Epiphyllum ackermannii'' (Cactaceae)|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.2307/1220912|journal=Taxon|volume=38|issue=1|pages=124–128|doi=10.2307/1220912|jstor=1220912 |issn=1996-8175|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Disocactus ackermannii.jpg|thumb|left|Close-up of the pistil and stamens]]
The stems of ''Disocactus ackermannii'' consist of a short rounded base, about {{convert|10|-|18|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} long, followed by longer flattened leaf-like portions, {{convert|10|-|75|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} long and {{convert|5|-|7|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} wide with wavy edges. The plant branches from the base and arches downwards, being altogether some {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on|0}} long. The scarlet flowers have greenish throats and are funnel shaped, {{convert|11|-|15|cm|in|abbr=on}} or even longer and up to {{convert|15|cm|in|abbr=on}} across. The filaments are red but the base is usually greenish. The anthers are pale rose. The style are red. The stigma is purplish. Fertilized flowers are followed by green to brownish red fruits, {{convert|4|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2|-|2.5|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} wide.<ref name=Ande01/><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Bravo-Hollis|first=Helia|title=Las Cactáceas de México|last2=Sánchez-Mejorada|first2=Hernando|publisher=Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México|year=1978|volume=1|location=México|pages=509–512|language=es}}</ref>

==Range and habitat==
''Disocactus ackermannii'' is native to the states of [[Chiapas]], [[Oaxaca]], [[Puebla]], and [[Veracruz]] in southern Mexico. It inhabits [[cloud forest]]s in the [[Sierra Madre de Oaxaca]] and [[Chiapas Highlands]] between 1,800 and 2,500 meters elevation.<ref name = iucn/>

==Taxonomy==
The species was originally named ''Epiphyllum ackermannii'' by [[Adrian Hardy Haworth]] in 1829. There are three sets of synonyms:<ref name=Ande01/>
* Haworth's ''Epiphyllum ackermannii'' was successively transferred to ''Cactus ackermannii'' (1830), ''Cereus ackermannii'' (1837), ''Phyllocactus ackermannii'' (1842) and ''Nopalxochia ackermannii'' (1935) before the current ''Disocactus ackermannii'' (1991).
* ''Phyllocactus weingartii'' <small>[[Alwin Berger|A.Berger]]</small> is an independent synonym.
* ''Nopalxochia conzattianum'' was named by [[Thomas Baillie MacDougall]] in 1947. It was successively transferred to ''Pseudonopalxochia conzattianum'' (1959) and ''Nopalxochia ackermannii'' var. ''conzattianum'' (1981) before the current ''Disocactus ackermannii'' var. ''conzattianum'' (1991).

Two varieties are currently recognized. ''D. a.'' var. ''ackermannii'' has longer [[cladode]]s (flattened stem portions), {{convert|35|-|75|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} long, and longer [[tepal]]s, {{convert|7|-|10|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} long. ''D. a.'' var. ''conzattianum'' has shorter cladodes, {{convert|10|-|50|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} long, shorter [[hypanthia]], {{convert|2.8|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, and shorter [[tepal]]s, {{convert|4|-|6|cm|in|abbr=on}} long.<ref name=Ande01/><ref name=":0" />

==Cultivation==
In cultivation, [[Disocactus × jenkinsonii|''Disocactus'' × ''jenkinsonii'']], a hybrid between ''[[Disocactus phyllanthoides|D. phyllanthoides]]'' and ''[[Disocactus speciosus|D. speciosus]]'', has been confused with ''D. ackermannii'' and is often distributed under the name "''Phyllocactus ackermannii''".{{sfn|ps=|Anderson|2001|p=226}}

''Disocactus ackermannii'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web 
| url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/327515/i-Disocactus-ackermannii-i/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Disocactus ackermannii'' | access-date=12 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 16 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 24 January 2018}}</ref>
